text:
maria: ran an nsys capture on the dedicated pool with a KV-cache heavy workload, seeing a ton of <no line info> in the kernel timeline for our runtime libs. stack traces are mostly unknown for libredwood_runtime.so and some cupti frames. attaching sample output inline:

maria: ```
nsys profile --output /tmp/trace.nsys \n  --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi \n  ./bin/redwood-server --workload kvcache-stress

# in timeline view: many frames collapsed as "unknown" or just symbol addresses
# nsys-cli shows: "no debug line info for /opt/redwood/lib/libredwood_runtime.so"
```

maria: I built with -g and kept the unstripped artifacts in the build image, but once I run inside our distroless-based runtime container the trace loses line info. tried mounting /usr/lib/debug from host, no luck.

ashok: can you paste the build-id from the binary?

maria: ```
readelf --note=.note.gnu.build-id -n /opt/redwood/lib/libredwood_runtime.so
  Owner: GNU
  Build ID: 3f2a1c6b9d4e5a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b
```

ashok: ok. nsys/prefetto typically relies on the build-id -> file mapping under /usr/lib/debug/.build-id/*/*.debug or on .gnu_debuglink. if those are missing inside container it falls back to addresses. check if your image strips or rewrites paths with -fdebug-prefix-map. sometimes that maps to an absolute path that doesn't exist in container. :thinking:

devon: we ran into this with the CUDA toolchain — CUPTI injects its own frames and can confuse addr2line if the lib path inside the trace doesn't match the container FS. two fixes that worked for us: mount the host debugstore or include the .debug files in the runtime image; or preserve the original source path via -fdebug-prefix-map to a relative prefix.

lina: also check for stripped cuda symbols. CUPTI has separate libs in /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64. if the trace refers to /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcupti.so and your image has a different soname, addr2line fails.

maria: tried running addr2line locally with the build-id, and it resolves when I point to the debug file on build host. inside container it fails. example:

maria: ```
# works on host:
eu-unstrip --build-id 3f2a1c6b9d4e... /opt/redwood/lib/libredwood_runtime.so /host/debug/3f/2a1c6b9d4e...debug
addr2line -e /host/debug/3f/2a1c6b9d4e...debug 0x7f4c12ab
# inside container returns "??"
```

samir: did you try setting NSYS_BASE or NSYS_DRIVER_DEBUG=1? nsight sometimes needs the runtime debug dir.

maria: I enabled NSYS_LOG_LEVEL=4, saw logs complaining about "failed to open file for build-id mapping".

ashok: another angle: our image build pipeline runs a dedupe step that canonicalizes paths and creates a new build-id (reproducible builds). if the debug info is generated before the path rewrite, the build-id in the stripped binary and the .debug file can mismatch. confirm the debug .debug file's build-id matches the binary inside container.

devon: quick repro we used earlier: build app -> strip -> move to distroless -> run nsys. If you avoid the strip (or include unstripped .debug alongside) the timeline shows line info. You can also ship .gnu_debuglink in the stripped binary pointing to relative debug file and include it in the image.

lina: for CUPTI specifically, set CUPTI_ENABLE_TRACING=1 and ensure the CUPTI lib in container has same buildid/soname. sometimes installing the system package for cupti (from cuda-toolkit) into the image fixes mapping.

maria: plan of action I'm trying now:
- mount /var/lib/debug/.build-id from CI artifact storage into container path used by nsys
- include a tiny wrapper that symlinks the host path referred to in the debug info into the container (fuzzy pathmap)
- fallback: run capture on a non-distroless debug image to confirm it's a packaging issue

perf-bot: New profile uploaded: s3://perf-traces/1987654321-kvcache-raw.nsys (size 92MB) :rocket:

ashok: one more trick: when building, add -fdebug-prefix-map=$(pwd)=/src to keep relative source paths. then when creating the debug image, ensure /src exists with the same tree or include a small mapping file. That prevents failing demangle/line lookup that uses original compile paths.

maria: update: mounting the host debugstore made nsys resolve most of the runtime symbols but still a few CUPTI internal frames remain unknown. looks like those come from a vendor-provided cupti build with no debuginfo.

devon: that's expected. vendor CU PTI rarely ships debug info. you can at least get function names by shipping an unstripped libcupti or using a local symbol server. For kernel-level hotspots from our runtime code you should be fine now.

maria: thanks — will push a debug image and re-run the KV-cache stress to validate batching heuristics hotspots. will paste results.

samir: if you want I can help make a temporary debug CI job that produces full .debug tarballs for any release. makes future traces easier to interpret.

maria: yes please. that would help a lot. :thumbsup:

ashok: also add a short README in our perf artifacts bucket describing how to map build-ids to debug files for on-call engineers. saved us a lot of time previously.

maria: noted. thanks all.
